description: Maps a sweep of control voltage onto the notes of a scale and fires a gate each time the note changes, for playing a ribbon or a touch strip like a harp

inputs.text: The notes of the scale to strum, 1V per octave, one per polyphonic channel, with channel 1 as the root; the format matches docB's Gen Scale and Aaron Static's ScaleCV
The position of the finger on the control surface; this is not 1V per octave but a plain sweep of voltage over the span set by Pitch CV Input Range
While this is at 1V or above the strum is sounding; with nothing patched the module strums without stopping

outputs.text: The pitch of the strummed note, 1V per octave, moving to the next of sixteen polyphonic channels each time the note changes so that notes can ring on
10V on the channel of the note being strummed and 0V on the rest, sixteen channels, moving to the next channel each time the note changes

notes: the two red readings show the root note of the scale at the top and the note being strummed underneath, and the bar down the right shows where in the range the strum is
with nothing patched to the scale jack the module uses eleven semitones from middle C and then repeats an octave higher, which is one note short of a chromatic scale
the number of notes the input span is divided into is set in the menu; it is 48 on a new module
menu: Number of notes mapped to the input CV pitch range — divides the input voltage span into that many steps, 2 to 48
Pitch CV Input Range — sets the voltage span expected at the pitch jack, from -10 to 10 down to 0 to 1
Sharps or Flats: Sharp, Flat — chooses how the two note readings spell an accidental

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads eleven semitones from middle C.
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · one channel only

unpatched it reads always strumming.
